text:
maya: Quick follow-up from the architecture sync — we need to pick a surface-level approach for in-flight request routing when data residency blocks serving from non-resident regions. Active/active is preferred for latency, but privacy constraints + KV/cache ownership complicate things. Thoughts?

aj: Two quick options I see: 1) strict-resident-only (reject/proxy to resident) or 2) resident-preferred with scrubbed fallback. each has pros/cons re: latency and audits.

sophia: Agree with aj. Also need a clear contract for what 'scrubbed' means. Compliance asked last week that raw prompts with PII never leave region X. That rules out naive fallback unless we strip content.

tarun: Stripping is doable in pipeline but risks changing model outputs (accuracy drift). For long streaming sessions (websockets) we also have to consider mid-session region swaps.

eva: To add, Dedicated customers might require 'never leave region' mode with hard enforcement. Hosted customers might accept scrubbed fallback. We should support both via flags on tenant config.

maya: Proposal: three-tier behavior per tenant: "resident-only" (hard block), "resident-preferred" (try resident, fallback to nearest with scrubbing), and "best-effort" (latency-first). Default = resident-preferred.

aj: Implementation notes: resident-preferred requires a short lease/ownership token attached to session metadata so a request can be proxied or redirected. Lease swap algorithm needs to avoid thundering herd.

sophia: Leasing idea ok, but we need drain semantics for streams. Suggest lease has states: active, draining, handed-off. When draining, accept only in-flight tokens that started before drain_ts.

infra-bot: deploy-check: routing-service v2 supports header X-Region-Affinity and X-Lease-Token but not drain-state yet.

maya: Good call. Also need audit trail: every time a fallback is used we log (in-region) a redacted snapshot + reason. Compliance-bot, does that satisfy audit?

compliance-bot: Redacted snapshot + reason logged in-resident-region meets baseline, but we also need a retention policy and proof-of-deletion when tenant requests. Include KMS key id in logs for tracing.

tarun: Operationally, proxying to resident region increases p95 latency a lot if resident region is far or overloaded. For resident-preferred, consider adaptive thresholds: attempt resident for up to 200ms, else fallback. Tunable per tenant.

eva: For Dedicated pools we can allow longer resident timeouts. For hosted small tenants, shorter. Add config flag: resident_timeout_ms.

aj: Edge case: what about KV cache hits that contain embeddings or context that cannot leave region? We can't shadow-copy those caches into nondesignated regions unless encrypted+tokenized. Alternative: remote KV fetch via async proxy with best-effort caching of non-sensitive keys.

sophia: Maybe classify keys as sensitive/non-sensitive during model onboarding. Non-sensitive keys can be replicated; sensitive keys only proxied. We will need a key classification API in the platform.

maya: Sounds like multi-piece plan: 1) tenant policy modes, 2) X-Region-Affinity + lease token + drain-state support, 3) resident_timeout_ms, 4) key-classification + selective replication, 5) redacted in-region audit logs. I'll draft a follow-up RFC with diagrams and state machine.

aj: +1 for RFC. Please include failure modes: split-brain on lease swap, cascading proxy overload, and policy misconfig. Also perf numbers for resident proxy typical p95.

compliance-bot: Also include sample audit events and retention defaults (90/365/forever) mapped to tenant tiers.

maya: I'll take the RFC. ETA EOD Friday for a first pass. If anyone has quick experiments (proxy perf, scrubbing accuracy) ping me.

eva: I can run a small perf test on proxy latencies this week.

tarun: I'll sketch a minimal key-classification API in the RFC so we can iterate.

maya: Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
